outcome.answer: For mobile/edge MoE inference, DyMoE is the closest match: dynamically quantize experts according to importance, preserve more precision in sensitive layers, and prefetch experts to overlap I/O stalls. Its authors report lower latency and faster token generation on commercial edge hardware [2]. More generally, allocate higher bit-widths to experts that matter more: GEMQ estimates importance globally and fine-tunes routing for quantized experts [5], while AlphaQ assigns precision from expert weight-spectrum properties without calibration data [3]. DPA-MoE offers runtime flexibility by allocating weight chunks to routed experts using live router scores, trading a modest throughput overhead for improved quality at matched budgets [7]. The supplied papers discuss edge hardware, but do not specifically establish which approach or bit-width is best for mobile NPUs.
